doc.title: Nat Hentoff interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Corporate radio and Americana stations
summary: Clear Channel dominates radio while Americana networks keep roots music alive.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: That they sort of have a monopoly on what is —

There used to be these free-form FM stations. Some of them still may exist. Well there is a network sort of, although it’s not a formal network, of Americana or Roots music, and that’s where some of these good country players can still get an audience. But in terms of hearing them in a big city or even a medium-sized city, that’s all taken over now.
